channel.title: Personal News Feed — Technology & Science
channel.description: Personally scored technology & science articles curated by news-filter

item.title: Taiwan Develops Autonomous Drone Swarms to Counter China's Grey-Zone Tactics
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Taiwan working on autonomous drone swarms to counter China’s increasingly aggressive grey-zone military tactics
Taiwan’s Ocean Affairs Council is developing autonomous drone swarms to counter China’s grey-zone military tactics. The project, in its second phase, involves coordinating two fleets of 10 drones each through simulations. The goal is to aid the Coast Guard Administration in defending against China’s activities, including damage to undersea cables and surveillance of Taiwan-U.S. cables. Researchers programmed drones for 100-foot separation, leader-follower formations, and dynamic obstacle avoidance. The system will allow different drone types to divide tasks and plan routes for maritime surveillance. Testing includes hardware-in-the-loop trials and flight tests in real maritime conditions. The project focuses on three Western drones: Jump 20, V-BAT, and Flexrotor. The V-BAT, recently acquired from U.S. firm Shield AI, offers vertical takeoff and 12-hour endurance, suitable for non-aircraft carrier ships.

item.title: China's Pacific Cable Surveillance Raises Tech Risks
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: China’s snooping around Pacific undersea cables raises risks for Big Tech
US-owned undersea cables in the Pacific face heightened risks from Chinese activities, according to a new report. Chinese research ships have spent significant time surveying cable routes, while commercial vessels are under investigation for cutting cables in European and Asian waters. The report, published by the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission in September 2026, warns that China and Russia may use cable sabotage as gray zone tactics amid rising tensions. The study includes an interactive vulnerability index ranking cables by risk factors like depth, shipping traffic, ownership, proximity to China's exclusive economic zone, and connections to Taiwan. Taiwan's status as a geopolitical hotspot, with China's military maneuvers around the island, is highlighted as a key concern. The index aims to prioritize cables for sensor deployment and patrols to monitor threats.

item.title: Japanese Researchers Create Smartphone-Linked Sensor to Detect Toxic Water Contaminants
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: A tiny smartphone gadget can detect some of the nastiest chemicals in your water
Researchers at the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology developed a portable sensor that detects PFAS chemicals in water using molecularly imprinted polymers. The device, connected to a smartphone or laptop, measures electrical changes when PFAS molecules bind to its surface. It can identify PFOA and PFOS at concentrations as low as 1.11 and 1.63 parts per trillion, with recovery rates between 88% and 96% in tested samples. The technology uses screen-printed electrodes on repurposed fabric, enabling rapid, low-cost testing. PFAS, known as 'forever chemicals,' persist in the environment and are linked to health risks like cancer and immune issues. Traditional testing requires expensive lab equipment, but this sensor could enable home or field use. The prototype, described in Biosensors and Bioelectronics, can be adapted to detect other PFAS compounds. Researchers note further development and field testing are needed before widespread availability.

item.title: Researchers create protein design tool using natural language prompts
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
Researchers in China developed a protein design tool that uses natural language prompts to create proteins with specified functions. The tool requires lab testing to distinguish successful designs from failed attempts, though its success rate is not high. Hugging Face announced a similar DNA-level design tool. Current advanced protein design tools use a two-step process: first, users define constraints like molecular binding or amino acid arrangements, then an AI generates a protein shape meeting those constraints. A separate tool then fills in the amino acid sequence to ensure proper folding. The new tools aim to simplify protein design by eliminating the need for detailed structural knowledge, though they rely on experimental validation to refine results.

item.title: Japan Tests AI-Powered Chainsaw Robot for Rail Maintenance
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Japan experiments with autonomous AI chainsaw-wielding robots
JR East, Japan's largest railway operator, demonstrated a robot with a chainsaw arm mounted on a rail truck to clear tree branches blocking tracks. The machine, currently remote-controlled by a human operator, is part of the company's broader AI integration to improve safety and efficiency. Engineers have used the robot since March, but a TV crew captured its operation for the first time. JR East aims to make the robot autonomous using AI image analysis for obstruction detection. Labor shortages and safety concerns drive the adoption of such technology, with maintenance work shifting to daytime hours. The firm has previously deployed AI tools for disaster recovery and drone inspections. If fully autonomous, the robot could reduce labor demands and enhance safety in hazardous tasks. The project highlights Japan's aggressive AI adoption in infrastructure maintenance.

item.title: Firefox 159 fixes 167 security flaws, including 13 sandbox escapes
item.description:
Source: PCWorld
Firefox 159 addresses 167 security vulnerabilities, including 13 sandbox escape flaws. The update includes a default-enabled password tool in the sidebar and an AI-assisted Smart Window feature for tracking website changes. Mozilla reports 65 vulnerabilities were reported by external researchers, with Amy Burnett from OpenAI submitting seven. Security fixes include 97 use-after-free issues and 108 high-risk vulnerabilities. Firefox 159 is available for Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android. ESR versions 153.6.0 and 115.44.0 also received patches, fixing 145 and 80 vulnerabilities respectively. The ESR 115.44.0 supports older systems until March 2027. Firefox 160 is set for November 10th release.

item.title: Gemini Notebook Adds Built-In Recorder for Lectures and Meetings
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Gemini Notebook can now record lectures and meetings without the upload shuffle
Gemini Notebook’s mobile app now includes a built-in recorder for capturing lectures and meetings directly within the app. Users can record audio without switching to separate apps or uploading files afterward. Google highlighted classroom lectures and team meetings as primary use cases, but the feature also allows recording personal thoughts for later review. The interface shows elapsed time and includes a pause button for breaks. After recording, the audio becomes a source in Gemini Notebook, enabling users to ask questions about the content. For example, after a meeting, users can query which decisions were made and which questions remained unresolved. Recordings can be paired with photos of handwritten notes, such as equations, to supplement audio explanations. This helps when speakers omit details, like symbols on a board. Each recording is limited to one hour, requiring multiple sessions for longer discussions. Users are advised to test the feature with short recordings first and plan natural stopping points to avoid exceeding the time limit.

item.title: UK Considers Using EVs to Balance Grid
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: UK government is considering using EVs to help balance the grid
UK ministers are considering offering additional Zero Emission Vehicle credits to manufacturers that integrate vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology into electric vehicles. V2G allows EVs to both charge from and supply energy to the grid, potentially balancing renewable energy fluctuations and reducing peak demand strain. Supporters argue the technology could support the transition to renewables, with early trials showing benefits like disaster resilience. Critics warn that incentivizing V2G might lead to increased production of polluting petrol and diesel cars. Ben Nelmes of New AutoMotive cautioned that manufacturers should be rewarded only if V2G is actually used, not just installed. Renault and Volkswagen offer V2G services in France and Germany, while Octopus Energy’s Power Pack claims to save V2G drivers £620 annually. However, consumer adoption faces hurdles, as managing V2G requires complex systems and understanding energy tariffs. Vicky Edmonds of the Electric Vehicle Association noted that drivers are still focused on immediate costs and practicality, complicating widespread adoption.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: ChatGPT Adds iCloud Mail and Calendar Plugins for Users
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: ChatGPT finally gets the iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins users have been waiting for
ChatGPT now includes iCloud Mail and Calendar plugins, enabling users to search emails, check appointments, and manage schedules via the chatbot. The integration is available on all ChatGPT plans, including the free tier, across web, desktop, and iOS. Features allow users to find confirmation emails, check calendar conflicts, reschedule events, search messages from specific contacts, summarize conversations, draft replies, and update calendar entries. Setup requires connecting via Settings > Plugins, using app-specific passwords generated through Apple’s account settings. Mail plugin requires an @icloud.com, @me.com, or @mac.com email, while Calendar uses the primary Apple account email. Users must enter the generated password instead of their regular Apple password. The plugin only accesses emails stored in iCloud Mail, not Gmail or Outlook accounts linked to Apple’s Mail app.

item.title: AI Tools Enable Native PC Ports of Console Games
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Why native PC ports of console games are suddenly everywhere
Native PC ports of console games are now achievable using AI tools like Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) and advanced models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude 5.5. REA integrates binary analyzers, decompilers, and other tools into a unified system, streamlining reverse-engineering tasks. Developers previously spent months manually analyzing game code, but AI agents now automate tedious processes like tracking memory allocation and system calls. Projects like Modern Warfare 2’s decompilation required up to 700 billion tokens and three months of work. AI models handle complex instructions more reliably, reducing errors and time. While AI can hallucinate, developers verify results by comparing decompiled code to the original. REA’s efficiency allows agents to manage multiple tools simultaneously, eliminating the need for manual terminal navigation. The combination of improved AI capabilities and accessible hardware like Raspberry Pi has made full decompilation and recompilation feasible, enabling console games to run natively on PCs.

item.title: SK hynix-Owned Solidigm Plans $45B US Flash Memory Plant
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: SK hynix-owned Solidigm is plotting a new $45 billion flash memory factory for the US, report claims
SK hynix-owned Solidigm plans a $45 billion flash memory factory in the U.S., according to reports. The move aligns with U.S. government efforts to boost domestic chip manufacturing, driven by national security concerns. Solidigm’s Dalian plant produces NAND flash memory, but export restrictions on advanced AI components to China have created a black market. Smuggled Nvidia chips, including Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs, are reportedly used in Chinese data centers. Solidigm’s U.S. plant would require government approval to ship machinery, with total U.S. manufacturing investment potentially reaching $100 billion. The company cited global NAND market volatility, including surging demand for data center-grade memory, as a reason for canceling an IPO. Solidigm reported $75 billion in revenue and $60 billion in operating profit, warning memory shortages will persist through 2030. The shift toward data center memory has led to production cuts in consumer-focused memory, driving up prices globally.

item.title: Garena Launches Localized Free Fire India After Four-Year Ban
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Free Fire returns to India as Garena launches localized version four years after ban
Garena launched Free Fire India, a localized version of the battle royale game, four years after its ban in February 2022. The new version, available on Android and iOS, includes India-specific content, parental controls, and data hosted on Indian servers. The launch follows a three-year delay after Garena initially announced the project in September 2023. Free Fire was banned alongside 53 other apps over national security concerns, but its variant Free Fire MAX remained available. PUBG Mobile’s Indian version, BGMI, has struggled to match Free Fire’s popularity, with 77.4 million monthly active users versus BGMI’s 20.8 million. Garena’s head of operations in India, Vaibhav Das Mundhra, confirmed Free Fire MAX will coexist with the new version, allowing shared accounts and events. He cited collaboration with Indian authorities but avoided explaining the 2023 delay. Despite regulatory hurdles, India’s mobile gaming market grew 14.2% in Q2, with $106 million in revenue. Free Fire MAX continues in India’s esports scene, with teams competing at the Esports World Cup 2026. Animesh Agarwal of S8UL Esports highlighted the potential for players and creators in the game’s return.

item.title: Windows 11 Now Lets Users Disable Web Search in Start Menu
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Windows 11 search can now skip web results and focus on your PC
Microsoft is rolling out a feature in Windows 11 that lets users disable web search results in Start menu searches. The setting, available via Privacy & security → Search, allows toggling off web suggestions and Microsoft Store recommendations. The rollout began in August 2026 and is not yet universal. Disabling web search prioritizes local apps, files, and settings, as seen in tests where queries like 'increase text size' directly linked to system settings. However, disabling web search removes features like weather forecasts and arithmetic calculations, requiring users to open dedicated apps instead. The feature does not disable all web content, as linked accounts like OneDrive or Outlook may still appear. Microsoft does not plan to default-enable local search, leaving users to adjust settings manually. The change may benefit users focused on local file access but limits web-based shortcuts.

item.title: Palmer Luckey's BlueChip Laptops to Feature Starlink-Style Antennas
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Palmer Luckey Floats Attaching Starlink-Like Antenna to His US-Made Laptops
Palmer Luckey’s military tech company, Anduril, announced the BlueChip laptop line, set to debut next year as US-assembled devices with Qualcomm chips. Luckey proposed integrating phased array antennas, similar to Starlink satellite systems, into the laptops’ design. These antennas, which transmit broadband signals, could be embedded in the laptop’s top shell alongside solar panels and other features. The BlueChip line targets government, defense, and public safety users, aiming to provide satellite internet access for military operations. Starlink’s role in Ukraine’s wartime communications was highlighted. Dell and Apple have also filed patents for phased-array antenna integration. Dell’s 2024 patent describes a flip-out antenna panel, while Apple’s 2023 patent suggests an internal antenna aligned with a housing aperture, adjustable based on lid positioning.

item.title: Ryobi offers official parts website and factory outlet for repairs
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Ryobi has an official replacement parts store (and it’s not Home Depot)
Ryobi offers an official replacement parts website and factory outlet for its tools. The Ryobi Power Ordertree site allows users to search by part number, model, or keyword for items like batteries, adapters, and covers. While the site lacks detailed photos and descriptions, it provides affordable parts, with some items under $1. A phone number is available for assistance. Ryobi also operates Direct Tools Factory Outlet, selling refurbished tools at discounts. Users can purchase parts directly from Ryobi or via Home Depot, though shipping costs may add to expenses. The site lacks photos for most items, requiring precise part identification. Repairing Ryobi tools through official channels is cheaper than replacing them entirely.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: User creates prompt to make AI chatbots stop acting like a friend
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: One prompt made ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini stop acting like my buddy
A user developed a single prompt to streamline interactions with AI chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini by eliminating behaviors such as teasers, excessive detail, and attempts to sound human. The prompt combines three earlier instructions—'No Teasers,' 'Don’t Act Human,' and 'On a Budget'—into a 200-word guide emphasizing direct answers, efficiency, and clear prioritization. Testing showed improvements: Gemini reduced nested steps for apartment tasks, ChatGPT provided a concise prioritized list for website fixes, and Claude cleaned up task labels without flattery. The prompt can be applied via custom instructions in each platform's settings. The user notes the prompt helps avoid unnecessary elaboration and ensures responses focus on solving problems without emotional or verbose language.

item.title: Amazon launches new Alexa devices with smart home and camera features
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Gizmodo, TechCrunch, Digital Trends, How-To Geek Original headline: Amazon Unveils New Alexa Devices with Smart Home, Camera, and Photo Features
Amazon released new Alexa devices including the Echo Dot, Echo Studio with Home Camera, Echo Show 16, Alexa Photo Frame, and Echo Time. The Echo Dot serves as a smart home hub supporting Zigbee, Matter, and Thread protocols, and functions as a Wi-Fi extender. A Kids edition costs $109.99, while the standard model starts at $99.99. The Echo Studio with Home Camera includes a built-in camera for object identification and video calls, with a camera-free version priced at $219.99. The Echo Show 16 features a 16-inch display, 13-megapixel camera, and smart home dashboard capabilities, priced at $499. The Alexa Photo Frame curates photos using Alexa+ and syncs automatically, with a black model at $199 and wood versions at $229. The Echo Time smart clock offers gradual wake-up, sleep monitoring, and customizable alarms, with a Kids version at $209.99. All devices include privacy features like physical camera disable buttons. Amazon emphasized enhanced smart home integration, entertainment, and personalization through these updates. Prices and pre-order discounts vary across models.
item.source: Engadget, Gizmodo, TechCrunch, Digital Trends, How-To Geek

item.title: iPhone USB-C Port Connects to 13 Devices
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 13 things you can connect to your iPhone's USB-C port
iPhone USB-C ports support connecting 13 devices and accessories, including keyboards, mice, external drives, and cameras. Users can connect peripherals like Apple’s Magic Trackpad and Keyboard via adapters, enabling typing and mouse functions. Screen mirroring to external displays works with USB-C cables, though it only mirrors the screen vertically. External drives with APFS, exFAT, or FAT32 file systems can be accessed via the Files app, with high-bitrate ProRes video recording possible on Pro models. USB-C hubs provide additional ports and passthrough charging. Ethernet connectivity is achievable with adapters, prioritizing Ethernet over Wi-Fi. MIDI devices and microphones work with adapters, while game controllers from Sony, Microsoft, and 8BitDo are supported. Wireless options exist but may limit simultaneous charging. Most devices require adapters, with some exceptions like USB-C hubs and modern controllers. File system compatibility and adapter quality affect performance, with USB 3.0 drives needing proper cables for speed.

item.title: UEFI Firmware Flaw Enables Pre-OS Code Execution in Servers
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
A critical code-execution vulnerability in UEFI firmware affects nearly all servers globally. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, exists in the TianoCore EDK II codebase, used by major vendors like AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix. It allows attackers to execute malicious code before operating systems and firmware defenses like Secure Boot are active, exploiting a memory-corruption issue in the ICMP component. The vulnerability, discovered by Anthropic’s Alex Matrosov and Google’s Dan Holmes, was scheduled for coordinated disclosure in January. AMI released a patch last month, prompting TianoCore to issue a public advisory. While patches are available, updating millions of devices is complex. The flaw highlights ongoing challenges in securing firmware, as attackers could exploit it to deploy persistent malware. The discovery follows another recent code-execution vulnerability in PHP.

item.title: Amazon Launches Echo Show 16 with Glare-Reducing Nanomatte Display
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Amazon adds a glare-reducing nanomatte display to its new Echo Show 16
Amazon launched the Echo Show 16, its latest smart display featuring a 16-inch HD screen with a glare-reducing nanomatte finish. The display uses anti-reflective etching developed with Corning to minimize glare while maintaining color accuracy. The device is 40 percent thinner than the Echo Show 15 and includes an anodized aluminum frame. It features eight custom micro woofers and two tweeters for clearer audio in noisy environments. The new model also has a 13-megapixel wide-angle camera with a 17-foot facial recognition range for Visual ID. Alexa+ now generates real-time interactive content, such as shopping comparisons and travel planning cards. The Echo Show 16 includes Fire TV for streaming services and can function as a digital photo frame or smart home dashboard. It is available for pre-order at $500 (standard) or $570 (nanomatte), with a $100 discount. Optional stands cost $70 or $125. The device will ship later this year.

item.title: Industrial AI and Human Control Integrate for Adaptive Factories
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
Industrial AI and human control are merging to create adaptive factories that operate like living systems. Digital twins, enhanced by AI, now provide real-time adjustments and closed-loop execution, enabling plants to self-regulate through small, continuous changes. These 'living' digital twins integrate sensor data and predictive models, allowing AI to act autonomously while human operators define health metrics and monitor performance. Examples include Saudi Aramco’s refineries, where AI optimizes production with human oversight, and Nestlé’s energy-efficient dryers. SCG Chemicals reports 99% plant reliability using AI-driven twins. Despite progress, challenges remain: 65% of executives cite operational risk as a top concern, and only 23% of organizations report significant changes in AI-driven decision-making. Governance frameworks, like the EU AI Act and AVEVA’s responsible AI board, aim to balance autonomy with accountability. McGreevy of AVEVA notes that AI will likely follow the supervisory model of SCADA systems, with full autonomy limited to repetitive tasks. Human roles are evolving to focus on defining operational limits and interpreting AI insights, ensuring systems remain aligned with business goals.

item.title: Amazon Introduces Alexa Home Map for Smart Home Control
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: The Alexa Home Map is a visual way to see and control your smart home
Amazon introduced the Alexa Home Map, a 3D interactive interface for controlling smart home devices. Unlike existing tile-based apps, the map displays devices as animated icons on a digital blueprint of the home. Users can view lights, speakers, and security cameras in real time, with features like glowing lights and moving people visualized similarly to Tesla’s Driving Visualization. Setup requires entering an address and using LIDAR-equipped iPhones or Android devices to scan interiors, placing devices on the map. The feature will roll out in preview later this year on iOS, with Android support arriving in early 2027. It integrates with Alexa and Ring apps, allowing users to filter devices by type and switch between floors. Amazon emphasized the map’s dynamic updates and evolving capabilities over time.

item.title: UC Berkeley Professor Halts Graded Homework Over AI Cheating
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Fields Medal-winning UC Berkeley professor ends graded homework due to AI cheating
UC Berkeley professor Richard Borcherds, a Fields Medal winner, has stopped assigning graded homework, citing widespread AI use that makes it impossible to distinguish student work from AI-generated content. He now relies on in-person exams without electronic devices to assess student understanding. Borcherds argues that online exams are ineffective, as students use AI to boost scores, making grading for correctness counterproductive. He stated, 'Paying to grade AI-generated answers is a waste of time and money.' The issue emerged with the release of GPT-3.5 in 2022, as AI tools have improved to the point of being indistinguishable from human work. Researchers note significant score increases in unmonitored online exams, prompting some professors to switch to in-person finals. UC Berkeley has explored AI-detection software but found it unreliable, instead allowing professors to set their own AI policies in syllabi. Borcherds said he would be 'very relieved' if AI’s only impact is making grading homework harder.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Fix Windows File History to Restore Files
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Windows File History broken? How to fix it and restore your files
Windows File History may fail to back up files. Users can enable the feature via Control Panel by selecting a backup drive. If configuration issues occur, resetting File History by deleting specific folders in C:\Users\[username]\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\FileHistory can resolve problems. The Data and Configuration folders must be removed, though the latter requires disabling File Version Control. After restarting, Windows recreates these folders. To restore files, open File History and navigate to backed-up folders. Double-click files to copy them to the SSD. The backup files remain on the external drive even after configuration reset.

item.title: U.S. Marines join NATO Baltic Sea mission to protect undersea cables from sabotage
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: US Marines join NATO mission in the Baltic Sea to protect undersea cables from sabotage as Russia continues to lurk
U.S. Marines are deploying to the Baltic Sea as part of NATO's Enhanced Vigilance Activity Baltic Sentry operation to protect undersea internet cables and gas pipelines from sabotage. Around 40 Marines from Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune will provide advanced surveillance and reconnaissance support, including small Unmanned Aerial Systems and littoral sensors, to feed data to NATO. Finnish Navy Chief of Operations Capt. Johan Tillander noted the Marines' expertise in monitoring the Baltic Sea. Maj. Gen. Daniel Shipley emphasized the mission's goal of deterring hybrid threats through rapid deployment of specialized forces. The Baltic Sea is a critical area for undersea infrastructure, with two cables cut between Finland, Sweden, and Europe in 2024. Russia, though not explicitly named in the press release, is identified as a persistent threat, with over 500 incidents of Russian fishing boats near cables in the past four and a half years. Finland established a maritime surveillance center this year to monitor activity in the region.

item.title: Core 4 Solutions sells $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: IT vendor lists massive $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 300 racks of decommissioned GPUs
Core 4 Solutions is selling a 300-rack AI supercomputer on eBay for $59.7 million. The cluster includes 9,600 Nvidia A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, totaling 268,800 cores and 1.4 petabytes of memory. Despite newer Nvidia Blackwell and Vera Rubin architectures costing up to $7.8 million per unit, the A100 remains relevant for AI and research due to its availability and cost-effectiveness. The valuation estimates $28.1 million for key components, with additional costs for racks, cooling, and networking hardware. The listing includes free FedEx Ground shipping or local pickup, though logistics for 300 racks pose challenges. The cluster has attracted 11 views and one carted buyer, with the final sale hinging on shipping preferences. The sale reflects growing demand for AI infrastructure amid expanding data centers.

item.title: Discord to make public server conversations searchable on Google
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Discord’s next big feature could put your conversations on Google Search
Discord is rolling out a feature to make conversations from public servers searchable on Google and other search engines. The change will launch in two phases: summaries of conversations will appear on public web pages starting November 16, with full messages searchable by mid-December. The feature targets Discoverable Servers—public communities with at least 1,000 members existing for eight weeks or more—though private servers, direct messages, and group DMs are excluded. Users can disable the feature via Discord’s settings to prevent messages from appearing online, but previously shared content may remain cached. Server admins can also disable message visibility. The feature is disabled by default in the EU/EEA, UK, Canada, Brazil, Australia, and South Korea, and teen accounts are excluded. Discord aims to improve accessibility of information like gaming guides and troubleshooting advice, but the move raises privacy concerns.

item.title: iOS 27.2 Adds Podcasts Redesign and Siri AI Upgrades to CarPlay
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: iOS 27.2 brings two new features to Apple's CarPlay
Apple released iOS 27.2, introducing two key changes to CarPlay. The Podcasts app now features a New Episodes section for latest episodes and a Continue Playing section for resuming shows, replacing the previous Up Next tab. Siri AI on CarPlay gains the ability to recall past conversations, allowing users to reference previous chats like cafe recommendations. The assistant can also draw from additional data sources such as voicemails, Safari history, Calendar event attendees, and message-attached photos. A new monochromatic Music app icon replaces the red color, with dark mode variations. Some users report that the APTV feature for video playback no longer works on CarPlay after the update. Minor changes include adjustments to the Music app icon and potential compatibility issues with certain infotainment systems.

item.title: Firefox adds AI form-filling and website monitoring
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Firefox can now fill out boring forms and monitor websites for you
Mozilla has updated Firefox's Smart Window with AI features for form-filling and website monitoring. The form-filling tool reads selected tabs, like a portfolio or professional profile, to suggest answers for online forms. Users can click 'Fill from sources' on forms with four or more text fields, review suggestions, and submit manually. Personal details like name and address use standard autofill and remain on the device. The feature currently supports text fields, with dropdowns and PDF forms planned. The website monitoring tool lets users type '/watch' in the Smart Window chat, select up to five sites, and set daily or weekly checks. Tasks appear under the Tasks button with desktop alerts, though Firefox must stay open. Both features are available in the US and Canada beta, with global rollout planned. Tasks pause after 60 days and stop after 90 days of inactivity.

item.title: Sony Launches Transparent PS5 Controllers and Covers for 2027
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Sony Unveils Transparent PS5 Controllers and Console Covers for 2027 Launch
Sony announced the Prism Collection, a new PlayStation 5 accessory line featuring transparent DualSense controllers and matching console covers. The design draws from 1990s translucent aesthetics, offering Flare Orange, Emerald Green, and Graphite Gray options with a premium glossy finish. Preorders begin November 10, 2026, with availability February 4, 2027. Controllers retail at $84.99, covers at $74.99. TechRadar noted the prices exceed standard controllers but match other special editions. The collection includes three console covers for customization. Sony’s design team emphasized showcasing DualSense craftsmanship, as stated in a PlayStation blog post. The trend follows Microsoft’s translucent Xbox Series X and Asus’ ROG Xbox Ally X20. Sony designer Leo Cardoso said, 'We wanted to bring back the iconic see-through trend of the late ’90s in a fresh, modern way that complements the PS5’s industrial design.' The accessories target retro gaming fans and long-term PlayStation enthusiasts, with TechRadar predicting strong demand due to their unique appearance and cultural relevance.
item.source: The Verge, Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Startup Generates Power From Underwater Volcano, Faces Challenges Ahead
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: A Startup Just Pulled Electricity From an Underwater Volcano Off Oregon. The Next Step Is Much Harder
Endurance Energy, a Seattle-based startup, tested the world’s first subsea geothermal power plant at Axial Seamount, an underwater volcano 300 miles off Oregon. The Adélie test system generated 8.7 seconds of net-positive electricity, peaking at 16.5 kilowatts, proving technical feasibility. However, the demonstration faced issues like software glitches and a failed power cable, limiting sustained output. Founder Andrew Redd emphasized overcoming engineering challenges like corrosion and deep-sea maintenance costs to achieve commercial viability. Experts note subsea geothermal’s potential for clean, reliable power but warn of high risks. Endurance plans to test an upgraded version, Gentoo, this winter with deeper wells and improved cables. While Redd remains optimistic about replacing diesel with local energy, experts caution that long-term durability and cost remain critical hurdles for widespread adoption.

item.title: Crystal Lake’s Ratings Hint at Potential Season 2 Renewal
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Will These ‘Crystal Lake’ Ratings Be Enough for a Season 2?
Crystal Lake, the Friday the 13th prequel, scored 1.3 billion minutes watched in its first 11 days, ranking as Peacock’s fourth-best scripted original debut. It also placed No. 3 among streaming originals and first-season series during the week of October 19. NBCUniversal reported 1.8 billion earned impressions and 7.6 million video views in the first 11 days. Showrunner Brad Caleb Kane hinted at season two ideas, possibly exploring the Jarvis family or Crystal Lake’s residents. While Carrie, a competing horror series, secured a season two renewal with 1.26 billion viewing minutes, Crystal Lake’s survival of its finale—where Pam’s head is lopped off—leaves room for further storytelling. The show’s main characters, including Pam and Jason, survive, and the series has not yet reached the events of the original Friday the 13th film.

item.title: Jio shares jump 21% on India’s largest IPO
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Jio shares surge 21% in market debut after blockbuster India IPO
Jio Platforms surged 21% on its stock market debut after raising $3.2 billion in India’s largest and most subscribed IPO. Shares opened at ₹1,358, valuing Jio at ₹12.5 trillion, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company. The offering attracted over $77 billion in bids, with more than 13.8 million applicants. Jio, India’s largest telecom operator, serves over 540 million customers. Akash Ambani, Jio’s managing director, stated the company aims to become a global technology firm. Jio reported ₹300.5 billion in profit and ₹1.47 trillion in revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026, both up 15% year-over-year. The IPO proceeds will repay ₹275 billion in debt at Reliance Jio Infocomm. Jio previously raised $10.2 billion from Meta and Google in 2020. The IPO included only newly issued shares, with no existing investors selling.

item.title: AI Bots Influence Public Health Policy by Opposing Vape Bans
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: AI bots are now trying to sabotage public health policies, like banning disposable vapes
AI bots are being used to manipulate public health consultations, as revealed by a British Medical Journal analysis. During a 2023 public consultation on disposable vapes, 118,756 responses were submitted to the UK Department of Health and Social Care. Researchers found 76% of these were fraudulent, with 90,833 responses overwhelmingly opposing vape sales restrictions. When bot-generated answers were excluded, 79.6% of remaining responses supported restricting disposable vapes. The study calls this the first documented large-scale AI bot interference in public health policymaking. Researchers note the tactics mirror past tobacco industry lobbying, with coordinated submissions. The attack highlights growing risks of AI-driven manipulation in policy decisions. Global institutions warn of escalating AI-powered attacks on public systems. The origin of the malicious responses remains unidentified, but experts warn such campaigns will likely continue.

item.title: Amazon Launches Echo Time Smart Alarm Clock with Customizable Design and Privacy Features
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, Engadget
Amazon launched the Echo Time, a smart alarm clock with customizable design and privacy features. The device features a 3.2-inch touchscreen with hundreds of clock faces, including analog designs and seasonal themes. It lacks a camera and includes visual indicators for Alexa’s listening status, plus a button to disable microphones. Sleep-sensing features are optional. The Echo Time mimics natural light changes and integrates Alexa+ for voice commands. Its smart alarm uses temperature sensors, presence detection, and ultrasound to wake users during lighter sleep stages 10-60 minutes before a set time. Traditional alarms can be disabled. The device is available in Graphite, Glacier White, and Coral Pink for $199.99, with an adjustable stand for $39.99. A Kids version, powered by Amazon Kids+, is available in Galactic Grape and Cosmic Lime for $210, including a year of bedtime content subscriptions. The Echo Time carries the National Sleep Foundation’s SleepMark seal, emphasizing its focus on sleep health. The standard model targets adults, while the Kids version allows children to set alarms and customize clock faces under parental control.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Motion sensors enable smart home automations for lighting, alerts, and more
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 5 powerful smart home automations that require nothing but a motion sensor
Motion sensors can trigger smart home automations for lighting, alerts, and daily routines. A hallway light automation adjusts brightness based on time of day, using full brightness in the evening and dim settings at night. A kitchen motion sensor detects morning activity, triggering a smart speaker to deliver a daily briefing with weather, school lunch details, and calendar events. Automations also manage dashboard screens by turning them on when motion is detected and off after a delay. Mailbox motion sensors notify users of delivered mail via phone alerts or speakers, sometimes faster than USPS email notifications. Presence sensors offer better detection for stationary users, but motion sensors suffice for many tasks like pantry lighting with cooldown timers. These automations enhance convenience without requiring complex setups.

item.title: Nvidia's Vera CPUs now available as standalone instances on Oracle Cloud
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Standalone Nvidia Vera CPUs land in Oracle Cloud's multi-gigawatt deployment
Nvidia and Oracle announced general availability of Nvidia’s Vera Rubin NVL72 rack and Vera CPUs on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Superclusters. This follows Google Cloud’s recent release of Vera, marking Nvidia’s first standalone CPU push into hyperscale data centers. Oracle’s deployment highlights Vera’s standalone instances, distinct from neoclouds like Nscale and CoreWeave. Vera’s memory bandwidth, up to 1.2 TB/s, outperforms dual Intel Xeon 6980P systems in benchmarks like Stream, with LPDDR5X-9600 and distributed mesh caching. While AMD and Intel lead in single-socket density, Vera’s topology adapts to workloads, showing strength in agentic AI tasks and Python performance. Oracle’s cautious approach includes offering HGX NVL8 clusters with eight Rubin GPUs. Vera’s versatility extends beyond AI, with potential in general data center workloads like SQLite queries, leveraging Nvidia’s Scalable Coherency Fabric. The deployment signals growing demand for Vera beyond GPU-centric use cases.

item.title: UK Launches Warm Homes Loan Scheme for Solar and Heat Pumps
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: UK homeowners can get interest-free or cheap loans for solar or heat pumps
The UK Government launched the 'Warm Homes Loan Scheme' to provide interest-free or low-interest loans for solar panels, batteries, and heat pumps. Homeowners can access up to £15,000 for solar and batteries, £20,000 for air-to-water heat pumps, and £35,000 for ground-source systems. Loans offer up to 5% lower interest rates than standard loans, with repayment terms up to 30 years. Energy suppliers like British Gas and lenders such as Tandem Bank and The Money Co-op are involved. The scheme also allows access to £9,000 grants under the Boiler Upgrade Scheme for heat pumps, though grants may be scaled back in future budgets. The Government claims loans will help households save up to £550 annually on energy bills. Analysis notes the loans are welcome but highlights potential changes to grants, which may shift focus to remote areas without gas connections. The scheme is available nationwide, including Scotland, where such loans were previously unavailable.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Acer Predator Atlas 8 launches in US at $1,300 with sold-out pre-orders
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: The $1300 Acer Predator Atlas 8 handheld is finally US-bound, and its pre-orders are already sold out
Acer's Predator Atlas 8 handheld gaming device is set for US release on November 1 at Best Buy for $1,299.99. The device features an Intel Arc G3 Extreme processor, 24GB LPDDR5X memory, 512GB storage, an 8-inch 120Hz touchscreen, and dual Thunderbolt 4 ports. It runs Windows 11 with Xbox Game Pass support and includes PredatorSense controls. The price positions it as a premium option above mainstream handhelds like the Steam Deck OLED and Nintendo Switch 2. Pre-orders for the US launch have already sold out, with online orders reopening on November 1. The device's performance advantages over competitors like the ROG Xbox Ally X20 likely contributed to its rapid sell-out.

item.title: Kodiak AI Signs First Commercial Deal for Public Highway Driverless Trucks
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Kodiak lands first commercial deal to supply driverless trucks for public highways
Kodiak AI will deliver 75 self-driving trucks to DTL Transport starting in 2028, marking its first binding commercial deal for driverless big rigs on public highways. The contract, announced Wednesday, precedes Kodiak’s plan to remove human safety operators from cabs by December 2028. DTL, a California trucking company, will use the trucks on routes including Dallas to El Paso and Interstate 20 between Dallas and Atlanta. Kodiak founder Don Burnette highlighted midmarket carriers’ agility in integrating self-driving technology. The deal could boost Kodiak’s revenue and support its shift to an asset-light model, licensing technology rather than owning trucks. DTL is Kodiak’s first on-highway DaaS customer, following a pilot program in California where the company autonomously hauled perishable goods 225 miles. Kodiak’s 2025 investor presentation projects $11.2 million in annual recurring revenue from the deal once all 75 trucks are operational. The company currently operates under a trucking-as-a-service model with customers like Charger USA and Werner Enterprises, but aims to transition to driver-as-a-service by licensing its technology for per-mile fees.

item.title: Smart Patch Monitors Workout Form via Wearable Sensor
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: A tiny smart patch could help you get your workout form right
A research team at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar, led by Dr Biswajit Saha, developed a flexible wearable sensor patch to help users maintain proper workout form. The patch, worn on key body parts, detects movement by measuring changes in electrical resistance and transmits data via Bluetooth to a phone. A machine-learning model compares the user's movements to reference data from trainers, coaches, and elite athletes, analyzing speed, force, and consistency. The device is designed to complement, not replace, personal trainers, as it cannot account for individual body differences or fatigue. Trials involve 50 gym users and 30 athletes in sports like tennis and swimming. The prototype has reached Technology Readiness Level 5, with a patent application pending. Results remain unpublished, and the team seeks industry and government partners to commercialize the product. If successful, the patch could provide real-time form feedback for solo workouts.

item.title: Virgin Galactic's Apeiron spaceship delayed to 2027
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Here’s Virgin Galactic’s new Apeiron spaceship
Virgin Galactic's new Apeiron spaceship, selected via public vote, is the first Delta-class craft but faces delays. The company now plans to launch Apeiron in mid-2027, over two years after its last commercial flight in June 2024. The first commercial spaceflight is expected in early Q2 2027, with the second spacecraft following in late Q2/early Q3 2027. Delays stem from extended avionics software integration and validation testing, which will occur at Spaceport America. Apeiron is currently en route to the spaceport via a captive-carry flight with its Eve launch vehicle. The updated timeline reflects thorough testing requirements before flight tests commence. Virgin Galactic retired its VSS Unity spacecraft in 2024, marking the end of its previous fleet. The Apeiron's journey to Spaceport America underscores the company's focus on ensuring software readiness for commercial operations.

item.title: FCC clears Amazon Leo to acquire mobile-satellite operator Globalstar
item.description:
Source: Engadget
The US Federal Communications Commission approved Amazon Leo's $11.5 billion acquisition of mobile-satellite operator Globalstar. The deal aims to expand Leo's space-based services and enable direct-to-device connectivity for its satellite network. The FCC stated the merger would enhance data coverage in underserved areas and create a stronger satellite operator offering fixed and mobile services. Globalstar, which provides Apple's emergency satellite connectivity for iPhones and Watches, had a 20% stake held by Apple prior to the takeover. Leo, competing with SpaceX's Starlink, currently has 400 satellites in orbit and plans to launch high-quality satellite internet in Uzbekistan. The company is partnering with Delta to provide in-flight satellite internet and has scheduled six Arianespace launches to deploy over 3,000 low-earth orbit satellites, significantly expanding its network.

item.title: Adobe charges $840/year for Creative Cloud; open-source project offers free alternative
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: Adobe wants $840 a year for Creative Cloud. This open-source project is recreating it for free
Adobe charges $840 per year for Creative Cloud subscriptions, with first-year promotions bringing the cost to around $740 annually. ArtCraft, an open-source project, aims to replace Adobe's Creative Suite with free alternatives. The project, in alpha stage, includes apps like PhotoCraft (Photoshop), VectorCraft (Illustrator), and FilmCraft (Premiere Pro), among others. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, with local-first design eliminating cloud dependency. While many apps support basic workflows—such as layers, masks, and RAW editing—full feature parity with Adobe tools is not yet achieved. Limitations include lack of third-party plugin support and incomplete export capabilities. Developers note the apps are not ready for professional replacement but offer a familiar interface. Users can access ArtCraft via GitHub or the GetArtCraft website, with browser and installable versions available. The project, while promising, remains an early-stage effort with ongoing development.

item.title: TikTok Launches Restaurant Guide Feature 'Must Eat'
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: TikTok expands into restaurant guides with ‘Must Eat’ feature
TikTok launched a new restaurant guide feature called 'Must Eat' to help users discover local dining options. The community-driven tool aggregates recommendations from over 40 million posts and comments, organizing them into categories like 'Everyday Eats' and 'Elevated Dining.' Users can filter results by cuisine, price, rating, and location. The feature allows direct bookings via OpenTable and is initially available in New York City, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. TikTok positions the tool as a competitive alternative to platforms like Yelp and Google Maps, leveraging its existing strength in user-generated content for restaurant discovery. The 'Must Eat' section is accessible through the app's search bar, Local feed, restaurant pages, and video links featuring participating eateries.

item.title: Matic's Serene Robot Vacuum Targets Noise-Sensitive Users
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Matic’s new Serene robot vacuum is designed for people who hate noise
Matic's new Serene robot vacuum claims to operate at 52 decibels, quieter than a refrigerator, while maintaining maximum suction. Priced at $1,695, it is $200 more than Matic's current model. The vacuum's noise level is three decibels lower than the original Matic, allowing users to avoid choosing between cleaning power and quiet operation. Mehul Nariyawala, Matic's cofounder, stated the Serene is designed for noise-sensitive individuals, featuring the same camera-based navigation and design as the original. Owners can upgrade existing Matic units to Serene by 2027, paying the difference between their original purchase price and $1,695. Those who bought the original at $1,095 would pay $600 for the upgrade. The Serene aims to appeal to users deterred by traditional robot vacuums' noise levels.

item.title: Meta Launches AI Pet Journal App in Philippines
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Meta’s next cute attempt at forcing AI into your life is an AI pet journal app
Meta launched Waddle World, an AI pet journal app available in the Philippines for adults. The app allows users to chat with a virtual pet, which creates journal entries and doodles based on daily updates. Weekly emails summarize user interactions. Mini-games like stacking groceries or spelling words earn points for virtual rewards. Meta clarifies Waddle World is not a productivity tool but a digital pet for casual engagement. The app aligns with Meta’s strategy to make AI more approachable, alongside projects like Muse AI and the Charm gadget. Expansion to other countries has not been confirmed. The free app is accessible via iOS and Android in the Philippines only.

item.title: Bank of America Warns Against Sharing Banking Passwords with AI Assistants
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Bank of America kindly asks that you don’t share your banking password with your AI assistant
Bank of America warns customers against sharing banking credentials with AI assistants. In an email titled 'Protecting your finances in the Al World,' the bank urges users to never disclose usernames and passwords to AI agents or third-party services. The email highlights risks such as unauthorized financial actions, account lockouts, and potential data leaks from AI security flaws. Banks are still navigating how to integrate AI tools for tasks like automated payments while preventing unauthorized access. A spokesperson confirmed the authenticity of the email shared online. The bank emphasizes customer responsibility, stating account agreements hold users accountable for activities resulting from shared credentials. If customers share login details, they risk financial loss and are legally liable for any resulting actions.

item.title: Apple Raises iPad and Mac Trade-In Values With New Releases
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: iPad, Mac Trade-In Values Get Major Boost With New Releases
Apple raised trade-in values for existing iPad and Mac models alongside new product releases. iPad trade-ins saw increases of $10 to $20, with entry-level models gaining $20 and iPad Pro/Air getting $10 and $15 respectively. Mac trade-ins saw larger boosts, with Mac Pro, Mac Studio, and MacBook Pro values rising by $365, $240, and $120. Other Mac models received $25, $55, and $90 increases. The changes follow steep price hikes in consumer electronics driven by AI infrastructure demand. Maximum values vary based on device configuration, age, and condition. Actual trade-in amounts may differ from listed maxima.

item.title: Audio Technica Launches First Wireless StreamSet Headphones
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Audio Technica just released its first set of wireless StreamSet headphones
Audio Technica launched its first wireless StreamSet headphones, the ATH-M50xSTS-WL. The model connects via 2.4GHz using a USB transceiver for low-latency audio, targeting content creators, streamers, and gamers. It offers 24 hours of battery life via USB charging, with wired use possible during charging. Features include adaptive noise cancellation with two levels, a cardioid condenser microphone that mutes when flipped, and 45mm drivers from the ATH-M50x studio monitors. The headphones include interchangeable earpads for sound quality and breathability. Priced at $299, they are available now. The design mirrors the wired ATH-M50xSTS model, with microphones based on Audio Technica's 20 Series. The company emphasizes the transceiver's role in minimizing latency for real-time applications like gaming and streaming.

item.title: Gartner: Only 3% of Companies Achieve AI Productivity Goals
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Gartner report finds just 3% of organizations say they've hit productivity and savings goals from using AI
Gartner's report states only 3% of organizations have achieved productivity and cost-saving goals from AI implementation. Despite widespread expectations and significant spending, most firms face challenges. Three quarters of leaders anticipate AI's impact, with 85% planning to increase 2027 investments. However, 38% are already over budget. CV Viverito, Gartner's senior director analyst, notes organizations lack cost savings from AI but highlight opportunities to shift employee focus to new capabilities. Gartner advises targeting AI efforts for tangible impacts and broadening adoption across all levels. Viverito adds capacity for AI exists but struggles with usability and redirecting it to value. A top economist warns AI benefits remain limited to tech firms, with corporate America seeing no financial returns outside the sector.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Reddit Introduces 'For You' Feed to Boost Discovery
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the ‘For You’ feed
Reddit introduced a 'For You' feed alongside its existing 'Following' feed, combining community posts with interest-based recommendations. The new feed aims to help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not otherwise encounter. Reddit claims the change will encourage broader engagement and align the platform with recommendation-driven social media trends. The feature is rolling out globally, allowing users to switch between feeds. While some users expressed frustration during testing, the company emphasized the 'For You' feed as a step toward fostering a 'more human internet' through novel discoveries. The update joins platforms like Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook in adopting similar recommendation systems. Reddit noted that while recommendations have existed before, the new layout gives them a dedicated homepage feed.

item.title: New study challenges comet role in Earth's life origins
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Did comets help life begin on Earth? New simulations challenge the idea
A Cambridge-led study challenges the idea that comets reliably delivered life's ingredients to Earth. Published in Scientific Reports, the research found that fragile organic molecules like hydrogen cyanide would likely be destroyed during comet impacts. Lead researcher Richard Anslow and colleagues previously proposed that gravitational interactions could slow comets, improving survival chances. The new study tested this in our solar system, combining comet evolution models with atmospheric entry simulations. Earth-bound comets generally arrived too fast and at steep angles, limiting molecule survival. Hydrogen cyanide, commonly found on comets, was used to test delivery feasibility. Surviving molecules would need to accumulate in useful concentrations, but opportunities were limited in Earth's early history. Comet impacts declined rapidly during the planet's first 500 million years. Asteroid impacts and Earth's own chemical processes are presented as alternative sources for life's ingredients. Mars offered marginally better comet delivery odds, but success remains unconfirmed. The study highlights a gap between detecting life's ingredients on comets and proving they contributed to life's origin.

item.title: Amazon Warns Against AI Token Inflation to Boost Productivity
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Amazon tells engineers to stop ‘tokenmaxxing’ to look productive
Amazon has issued new engineering guidelines warning against 'tokenmaxxing,' where employees inflate AI usage metrics to appear productive. The October 27 memo states that higher token consumption does not guarantee better outcomes, urging managers to focus on long-term results instead of metrics like token counts, code changes, or reviews. The company argues that disconnected metrics encourage wasteful behavior, increasing compute costs and software complexity. Amazon emphasizes using usage data alongside other indicators to assess AI adoption's impact. The guidance follows reports of employees using internal tools like MeshClaw to artificially boost token counts. Amazon has not imposed token caps but shut down an internal leaderboard after employees gamed it. The push aligns with CEO Andy Jassy's push to integrate AI into operations, though he acknowledges automation may reduce corporate roles. Other companies like Uber and Accenture also face challenges with rising token costs, with Uber’s Andrew Macdonald noting higher usage hasn’t translated to consumer benefits yet. OpenAI’s Sam Altman has called token costs a major issue as firms struggle with escalating AI expenses.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: 3D printing simplifies home improvement projects during rainy weekends
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 5 home-improvement 3D prints that make a rainy weekend feel productive
3D printing enables home improvement projects during rainy weekends. Cabinet pulls can be 3D printed with drilling jigs for precise installation, avoiding the need for professional tools. Replacement parts for discontinued items like dishwasher clips or vacuum motor supports can be printed using calipers and design software, with PLA or PETG materials recommended based on heat exposure. Custom drawer dividers, such as Gridfinity systems or simple 3D-printed bins, help organize kitchen junk drawers. Wall systems like MultiBoard offer customizable storage solutions, with PETG, ABS, or ASA suggested for high-heat areas. Painting projects benefit from 3D-printed painter’s pyramids, pour spouts, and dust catchers. These projects leverage affordable filament and design tools to address common home maintenance tasks.

item.title: US satellite captures Chinese spaceplane in low-Earth orbit
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: China's top-secret spaceplane can't hide in low-Earth orbit
A Chinese spacecraft resembling the US X-37B spaceplane was photographed in low-Earth orbit by a US-owned commercial satellite in 2024. The image, captured by Vantor (Maxar), shows the Chinese vehicle with delta wings, payload bay doors, and a rear-mounted service module similar to the X-37B. The US Space Force revealed Maxar’s observation at a 2024 conference but withheld the full-resolution image until a Defense Intelligence Agency report was released. China has launched four spaceplane missions since 2020, with one currently in orbit after a February launch. The DIA report notes China’s spaceplane missions last up to nine months, though details remain undisclosed. The US operates two X-307Bs with missions lasting up to 2.5 years, though most activities are classified. The Chinese spaceplane’s design and capabilities mirror the X-37B, raising concerns about orbital operations and potential military applications.
